title: Mutual NDA playbook (ContractNLI layer)
provenance: Written 14 October 2026 for the ContractNLI layer of the benchmark. One rule per ContractNLI hypothesis (Koreeda & Manning 2021; the hypotheses are theirs, the positions are ours). Positions take the balanced, mutual stance of the Common Paper Mutual NDA and oneNDA: broad confidential information including oral disclosures, use limited to the purpose, need-to-know sharing with representatives, the standard exclusions, limited retention. Written before any model was run on this layer and not tuned to results. Not legal advice; not lawyer validated. Rule IDs map to hypotheses in rules.mjs. Version 2 (14 October, after the first calibration run on the development split): NDA-11 acceptable position changed from "silent and no tangible materials or software are exchanged" to "silent", because the conditional wording made the reviewer flag the omission in 29 of 61 NDAs; no other change.

rules.title: How confidential information is identified
rules.guidance: Confidential information should be protected whether or not it is marked. A regime that protects only information the discloser has expressly identified or marked as confidential leaves oral disclosures and unmarked documents unprotected.
rules.preferred: Information is confidential if it is marked as such or if a reasonable person would understand it to be confidential from its nature or the circumstances of disclosure.
rules.acceptable: Marking required for written material, with oral disclosures protected if identified as confidential at the time or confirmed in writing within a set period.
rules.escalation: Protection limited to information expressly identified or marked by the discloser, with no catch-all for information that is obviously confidential.

rules.title: Scope of confidential information
rules.guidance: Confidential information covers business, financial, commercial and personal information as well as technical information.
rules.preferred: A broad definition covering all non-public information of the discloser, in any form.
rules.acceptable: A definition listing categories, provided business and commercial information are included alongside technical information.
rules.escalation: Confidential information limited to technical information only (designs, code, specifications, know-how) with business information excluded.

rules.title: Oral and visual disclosures
rules.guidance: Information conveyed orally or by demonstration is confidential on the same footing as written information.
rules.preferred: Confidential information expressly includes information disclosed orally, visually or by demonstration.
rules.acceptable: Oral disclosures protected if identified as confidential when made, or summarised in writing within a reasonable period.
rules.escalation: Oral or visual disclosures excluded from protection, or protection limited to written and electronic material.

rules.title: Use limited to the purpose
rules.guidance: The receiving party may use confidential information only for the purpose stated in the agreement. A residuals clause, or any right to use the information for the recipient's own products or other purposes, defeats the agreement.
rules.preferred: Use restricted to the stated purpose; no other use without the discloser's written consent.
rules.acceptable: Use for the purpose and for internal evaluation directly connected to it.
rules.escalation: Any wider right of use, including a residuals clause allowing use of information retained in unaided memory.
rules.hardLine: A right to use confidential information for any purpose.

rules.title: Sharing with employees
rules.guidance: The receiving party must be able to share confidential information with its own employees who need it for the purpose, provided they are bound by confidentiality obligations.
rules.preferred: Disclosure permitted to employees and officers with a need to know, bound by obligations no less protective than the agreement.
rules.acceptable: Disclosure to named or approved employees, or to employees who have signed an acknowledgement.
rules.escalation: No disclosure to any employee without the discloser's prior written consent, or a prohibition on any internal sharing.

rules.title: Sharing with advisers and other representatives
rules.guidance: Professional advisers, consultants, agents and affiliates engaged for the purpose need access on a need-to-know basis, bound by equivalent confidentiality obligations, with the receiving party responsible for their compliance.
rules.preferred: Disclosure permitted to representatives (affiliates, advisers, consultants, agents) with a need to know, bound by obligations no less protective, the recipient remaining liable for them.
rules.acceptable: Disclosure to professional advisers bound by professional duties of confidence, and to other third parties with the discloser's consent not unreasonably withheld.
rules.escalation: No disclosure to any third party in any circumstances without prior written consent at the discloser's sole discretion.

rules.title: Compelled disclosure
rules.guidance: Where the receiving party is required by law, regulation or court order to disclose confidential information, it should give the discloser prompt notice (where lawful) so the discloser can seek protection, and disclose only what is required.
rules.preferred: Prompt written notice before compelled disclosure where legally permitted, reasonable cooperation in seeking a protective order, disclosure limited to what is legally required.
rules.acceptable: Notice where practicable and lawful, without an obligation to resist the order.
rules.escalation: Compelled disclosure permitted with no obligation to notify the discloser.

rules.title: Confidentiality of the agreement and discussions
rules.guidance: The existence of the agreement and of the parties' discussions is itself confidential unless the parties agree otherwise.
rules.preferred: Neither party discloses the existence or terms of the agreement or the fact of the discussions without the other's consent.
rules.acceptable: The agreement is silent on the point, or permits disclosure of the agreement's existence (but not its subject matter) to advisers and as required by law.
rules.escalation: A right for one party to publicise the relationship or the discussions.

rules.title: Reverse engineering
rules.guidance: Where samples, prototypes, software or other objects embodying confidential information are provided, the receiving party must not reverse engineer, decompile or analyse them to derive the confidential information.
rules.preferred: An express prohibition on reverse engineering, decompiling or disassembling any materials or objects embodying confidential information.
rules.acceptable: The agreement is silent on reverse engineering.
rules.escalation: An express right to reverse engineer or analyse materials provided.

rules.title: Independent development
rules.guidance: Information the receiving party develops independently, without use of or reference to the confidential information, is excluded from the obligations. This is a standard exclusion that protects the recipient's existing and future work.
rules.preferred: An express exclusion for information independently developed without reference to the confidential information.
rules.acceptable: The agreement is silent on independent development.
rules.escalation: An express statement that independently developed information is nonetheless covered, or a prohibition on developing similar information.

rules.title: Information from third parties
rules.guidance: Information lawfully received from a third party who is not under a duty of confidence to the discloser is excluded from the obligations.
rules.preferred: An express exclusion for information lawfully obtained from a third party without breach of any confidentiality obligation.
rules.acceptable: The agreement is silent on third-party sources.
rules.escalation: An express statement that information obtained from third parties remains confidential information under the agreement.

rules.title: No licence or transfer of rights
rules.guidance: Disclosure grants the receiving party no licence or other right in the confidential information or the discloser's intellectual property beyond the limited right to use it for the purpose.
rules.preferred: An express statement that no licence or other right is granted, and that all confidential information remains the discloser's property.
rules.acceptable: The agreement is silent on licences, with use confined to the purpose.
rules.escalation: Any grant of a licence or other right in the confidential information or the discloser's intellectual property.

rules.title: Return or destruction
rules.guidance: On termination or on request, the receiving party returns or destroys confidential information and copies, subject to the limited retention in NDA-20.
rules.preferred: Return or destruction on the discloser's request or on termination, at the recipient's option, with written confirmation if requested.
rules.acceptable: The agreement is silent on return or destruction.
rules.escalation: An express right for the recipient to keep all confidential information after the agreement ends, with no obligation to return or destroy on request.

rules.title: Copies
rules.guidance: The receiving party may make the copies reasonably necessary for the purpose, which carry the same confidentiality markings and obligations. A complete prohibition on copying is unworkable in practice.
rules.preferred: Copies permitted as reasonably necessary for the purpose, subject to the same obligations.
rules.acceptable: Copies permitted with the discloser's consent not unreasonably withheld, or limited to a stated number.
rules.escalation: An absolute prohibition on copying or reproducing confidential information in any form.

rules.title: Non-solicitation
rules.guidance: A confidentiality agreement should not carry restrictive covenants. A non-solicitation or no-hire clause binding one or both parties' employees belongs in a separate agreement with separate consideration, if anywhere.
rules.preferred: No non-solicitation, no-hire or non-compete provision.
rules.acceptable: A mutual non-solicitation limited to employees met through the discussions, for no more than twelve months, excluding general advertising.
rules.escalation: Any one-sided non-solicitation, any no-hire, or any restriction longer than twelve months.

rules.title: Survival of obligations
rules.guidance: Confidentiality obligations continue after the agreement ends, for a defined period or, for trade secrets, for as long as the information remains a trade secret.
rules.preferred: Obligations survive termination or expiry for a stated period of at least two years after the agreement ends, and indefinitely for trade secrets.
rules.acceptable: Obligations survive for a stated period of at least one year after the agreement ends.
rules.escalation: Obligations that end when the agreement ends, or that expire on a date regardless of when the information was disclosed, with no survival.

rules.title: Retention after return or destruction
rules.guidance: The receiving party may retain copies required by law, regulation or bona fide document-retention policy, and automatic electronic back-ups, provided they remain confidential. An absolute obligation to return or destroy everything, with no retention carve-out, is impracticable.
rules.preferred: Retention permitted to the extent required by law or internal compliance policy, and for routine back-ups, with the obligations continuing to apply.
rules.acceptable: Retention of one archival copy by legal counsel for compliance purposes.
rules.escalation: An absolute obligation to return or destroy all confidential information and every copy, with no retention of any kind.
